world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: A recurring supply chain turns cedar, graphite, clay, and pencil-making supplies into pencils that shops sell to customers.

actions.description: Saw cedar logs into pencil slats.
Supply clay for making pencil leads.
Mix graphite and clay into pencil leads.
Supply paint, erasers, brass ferrules, and shipping boxes.
Glue leads into wood slats, paint the pencils, and add erasers and brass ferrules.
The sawmill buys cedar logs from the logger.
The lead maker buys graphite from the mine.
The lead maker buys clay from the clay supplier.
The factory buys leads from the lead maker.
The factory buys wood slats from the sawmill.
The factory buys paint, erasers, ferrules, and boxes from the materials supplier.
The freight company carries packed pencil boxes from the factory to the shops.
The shop sells pencils to a customer.

mechanics.rationale: Cutting produces logs for the logger.
Sawing consumes logs and produces slats.

checks.label: the sawmill has enough cedar logs

mechanics.rationale: Mining adds graphite to the mine's available stock.
semantic_bindings: Mined material is recorded as graphite.

mechanics.rationale: The supplier adds supplied clay to its stock.
limits: The description gives no clay reserve.
semantic_bindings: Supplied material is recorded as clay.

mechanics.rationale: The lead maker consumes graphite and clay to make leads.

checks.label: the lead maker has enough graphite
the lead maker has enough clay

limits: One unit of each input per lead is a modeled recipe, not a stated ratio.
tests: Adequate inputs are consumed to make leads.

mechanics.rationale: The materials supplier supplies the four listed factory materials.
limits: The description specifies no inputs for these supplies.
tests: A positive quantity adds each listed supply.
semantic_bindings: The supplier stocks paint, erasers, ferrules, and boxes.

mechanics.rationale: The factory consumes the listed materials to assemble pencils.

checks.label: the factory has enough wood slats

limits: One unit of each listed input per pencil is an assumed recipe.
tests: Assembly consumes inputs and produces pencils.

mechanics.rationale: Packing consumes pencils and boxes and produces packed pencils.
limits: One box per pencil is assumed.
semantic_bindings: Pencils and boxes become packed pencils.

mechanics.rationale: The sawmill buys available logs from the logger and pays the listed price once.

checks.label: the logger and sawmill are in the same place
the sawmill can pay the logger's price

limits: Price is charged once per action. Parties must be colocated.
tests: Logs transfer and the listed price is paid once.

mechanics.rationale: The lead maker buys graphite from the mine and pays its listed price once.

checks.label: the mine and lead maker are in the same place
the lead maker can pay the mine's price

limits: Price is charged once per action; parties must be colocated.
tests: Graphite transfers and the listed price is paid once.
semantic_bindings: Graphite moves to the lead maker.

mechanics.rationale: The lead maker buys clay from the supplier and pays its listed price once.

checks.label: the clay supplier and lead maker are in the same place
the lead maker can pay the supplier's price

limits: Price is charged once per action; parties must be colocated.
tests: Clay transfers and the listed price is paid once.
semantic_bindings: Clay moves to the lead maker.

mechanics.rationale: The factory buys leads from the lead maker and pays its listed price once.

checks.label: the lead maker and factory are in the same place
the lead maker has enough leads
the factory can pay the lead maker's price

limits: The parties start in different places; the trade requires their locations to match.
tests: Leads transfer when parties are colocated.

mechanics.rationale: The factory buys slats from the sawmill and pays its listed price once.

checks.label: the sawmill and factory are in the same place
the factory can pay the sawmill's price

limits: The parties start in different places; the trade requires their locations to match.
tests: Slats transfer when parties are colocated.

mechanics.rationale: The factory buys all four listed materials from the supplier.

checks.label: the supplier and factory are in the same place

limits: The two parties start in different places; this transfer requires their locations to match. Cash payment is omitted because the four material transfers use the maximum effects.
tests: All four materials transfer when available and the parties are colocated.
semantic_bindings: The factory receives paint, erasers, ferrules, and boxes.

mechanics.rationale: The freight company delivers packed pencils from the factory to the shops; the transfer happens on arrival, after the shipment count reaches zero.

checks.label: the freight company is at the factory
the factory has enough packed pencils
the freight company has no shipment underway

limits: Shipment arrival and delivery cannot be represented accurately because the allowed paths do not include carrier cargo or a way to set the destination location; this action records dispatch only and does not move goods to the shops.
tests: Dispatch requires packed pencils and the carrier at the factory.
The requested destination must be the shops.
semantic_bindings: Dispatch subtracts packed pencils from the factory and marks a shipment underway.

mechanics.rationale: The shop sells one pencil per action, charges its listed price once, and serves one waiting customer order.

checks.label: the customer and shop are in the same place
the shop has a pencil to sell

limits: As required for priced sales, each action sells exactly one pencil regardless of quantity.
tests: One sale transfers one pencil, charges once, and serves one order.
semantic_bindings: The shop sells pencils to a customer.

processes.rationale: Renew source-side cedar log availability so cutting can continue.
Renew graphite at its represented source so mining can continue.
Renew clay at its represented supplier source.
Customers generate recurring demand so sales can continue after serving existing orders.
